status: Declared before first fitting execution; existing target results were already inspected
scope: New fits on frozen synthetic data; not new random trials or independent blind validation
information: Same 80 response observations, exact loadings, nonnegative unit-mass spectrum and upper rate cap 4. No generating rates, true noise amplitude or target responses enter fits/selection.
ridge_penalty: Squared L2 norm of positive-rate weights, excluding equilibrium; finite-grid representation-dependent regularization, not a continuum prior
selection: Last quarter of EACH loading record held out: 4 of 16 pilot samples and 8 of each 32 confirmation samples. Select ridge penalty / Prony order by mean squared response error on these 20 observations only. Refit all 80 observations. No target-score selection.
failure_policy: A failed solver is retained with its status. Do not label a nonconverged candidate successful. Select only successful candidates; report partial candidate failures, full refit failure and failed-start counts separately.
point_references: Midpoints of saved symmetric and classical continuous posterior intervals. They are explicitly point estimates, not guaranteed MSE optima.
tolerance_reason: Half the existing diameter thresholds 0.20 and 0.10; this is a fixed absolute point-error comparison, not a new claim about the prospective pair-diameter decision.
reporting: All cases and calibration-valid/invalid subsets separately, four families separately, windows paired. Count 256 cases, not 1024 independent replicates. Report accurate fitting baselines even if no failures or advantage occur.
stopping: Pilot checks arithmetic, constraint compliance, statuses and runtime, not superiority. Do not retune to create target errors. Full run proceeds after structural checks; complete negative findings are publishable evidence.
limits: No calibrated statistical intervals for fit baselines
Numerical multi-start is not a global optimum certificate
Fixed-grid minimum positive rate is a numerical restriction and cannot be attributed to continuum truth
No worst-case superiority inferred from mean prediction errors
